conditions.exact_rule_quote: sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises
conditions.description: The tenant must have sub-let, assigned, or otherwise parted with possession of the whole or a part of the subject-premises.
conditions.scope: Section 14(1)(b) core transfer/possession element under the supplied Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958 reproduction; historical-version scope remains unverified.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord
conditions.description: Any qualifying subletting, assignment, or parting with possession must have occurred without the landlord's written consent.
conditions.scope: Section 14(1)(b) written-consent requirement; the frozen inventory contains a landlord claim but no independently accepted fact establishing absence of written consent.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952
conditions.description: The qualifying transfer or parting with possession must have occurred on or after 9 June 1952.
conditions.scope: Temporal gate in the supplied statutory reproduction; the frozen inventory gives the 1974 filing date but not an express date for the alleged induction or transfer conduct.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: on an application made to him in the prescribed manner
conditions.description: The recovery proceeding must be on an application to the Controller made in the prescribed manner.
conditions.scope: Section 14(1) procedural gate. The inventory establishes a 1974 section 14 eviction proceeding but expressly leaves compliance with every prescribed procedural requirement unknown.

conditions.exact_rule_quote: The test of exclusive possession, though not conclusive, is a very important indication in favour of tenancy
conditions.description: For the supplied analogous licence-versus-tenancy inquiry, exclusive possession is an important but non-conclusive indication; retained control over the occupied part qualifies against treating occupation as tenancy or subletting.
conditions.scope: Analogous authority under the Delhi and Ajmer Rent Control Act, 1952. It may inform the control/exclusive-possession inquiry but does not replace section 14(1)(b) of the 1958 Act; the supplied source is incomplete.

bindings.stage: Additional Rent Controller decision dated 5 June 1997
bindings.reason: The Rent Controller found that the landlord had failed to show any subletting, assignment, or parting with possession; this is candidate contrary evidence for the core statutory transfer element.
The Appellate Tribunal found that the facts disclosed subletting to respondents 2 to 4; as a lower-forum finding it supports, but does not itself establish, the target element.

Admitted occupation of a portion of the premises by the three doctors is a candidate factual predicate for a possible parting-with-possession inquiry, but does not alone establish the legal character of that occupation.

bindings.stage: position described in judgment under Supreme Court appeal
bindings.reason: The landlord's stated position was that respondents 2 to 4 were inducted without written consent; because this remains a claim with the inventory expressly marking independent proof unknown, it is only candidate support.

bindings.stage: case history describing Rent Controller proceeding
bindings.reason: The reported institution of a section 14 eviction proceeding in 1974 supports the existence of a Controller proceeding, while the inventory expressly leaves full prescribed-manner compliance unknown.
The Rent Controller found respondents 2 to 4 were not in exclusive possession, which is candidate evidence against the exclusive-possession indicium.

The High Court found the Tribunal's exclusive-possession conclusion unsupported by evidence and based on surmises; this is candidate contrary evidence while preserving that it is a lower-court finding.
The High Court found that the tenant retained full physical and legal control and possession, which is candidate evidence against treating the doctors' occupation as exclusive possession.
The High Court characterized the doctors' presence as temporary and permissive while the tenant remained present, which is candidate evidence against exclusive possession.
The tenant respondents claimed that full control was never ceded and entry and exit remained under their exclusive control; as a party claim it is candidate contrary evidence only.

bindings.stage: Appellate Tribunal reasons quoted in Supreme Court record
bindings.reason: The retained Tribunal reasons treated the doctors as having an exclusive mezzanine-floor portion without tenant interference, which is candidate support for the exclusive-possession indicium.

bindings.stage: Appellate Tribunal reasons quoted in Supreme Court record
bindings.reason: The retained Tribunal reasons treated the doctors' use as exclusive during permitted practice periods and as more than a mere licence; this is candidate support while remaining a lower-forum finding.

target_refs.quote: we set aside the judgment of the High Court and restore the Appellate Tribunal’s findings.

element_targets.reason: The target court expressly restored the Appellate Tribunal's findings after holding that the High Court had impermissibly re-appreciated the evidence. Because the restored Tribunal finding was subletting to respondents 2 to 4, this is express target adoption of the core transfer/subletting finding without importing that conclusion into the frozen input.

The target judgment restores the Tribunal globally but does not separately and expressly decide the distinct statutory fact of absence of written landlord consent. Under the task's anti-inference rule, the overall disposition is insufficient to mark this element satisfied.

The target reasoning does not expressly identify when the doctors were inducted or when any qualifying transfer occurred relative to 9 June 1952. The 1974 filing date does not itself establish the date of the transfer conduct.

target_refs.quote: an eviction proceeding instituted under Section 14 of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958

element_targets.reason: The target record expressly describes a section 14 eviction proceeding, but does not expressly establish that every prescribed-manner requirement was satisfied. The frozen inventory itself flags that point as unknown.

target_refs.quote: The onus, under such circumstances, was on the respondents to establish the degree of control they were maintaining
individual cabins and had separate telephone connections

element_targets.reason: The target court treated the degree of retained control as material after admitted third-party occupation, identified the cabins and separate telephone connections as factors used by the Tribunal, and expressly restored the Tribunal's findings. This supports the control/exclusive-possession qualification at the target stage, while the supplied oracle authority remains only analogous.

target_refs.quote: we set aside the judgment of the High Court and restore the Appellate Tribunal’s findings.
The appeal stands allowed in the above terms.

issue_target.reason: At the target stage the Supreme Court expressly restored the Appellate Tribunal's findings and allowed the landlord's appeal. That supports the fixed section 14(1)(b) issue at the issue level, while separate statutory subconditions not expressly addressed remain UNRESOLVED rather than being inferred from the disposition.
